summary: Upgraded the ClientApp from Angular 8.1 to Angular 9.1 using `ng update` for @angular/core and @angular/cli, which also bumped TypeScript to 3.8, rxjs to 6.6 and zone.js to 0.10 and ran all of Angular's v9 migrations. NgRx was moved from 8.6 to 9.2 (via its own `ng update`) because NgRx 8 only peers with Angular 8. `npm install` and `npm run build` both pass; `npm test` still fails for the same pre-existing angular.json misconfiguration it failed with at baseline.
changes: Ran `ng update @angular/core@9 @angular/cli@9`; all six v9 core migrations (static flag, @Injectable, ModuleWithProviders, Renderer2, undecorated classes x2) ran and reported no source changes needed.
angular.json: CLI migration added `aot: true` to the browser build options (Ivy/AOT is the v9 default) and an `anyComponentStyle` budget to the production configuration.
src/tsconfig.app.json and src/tsconfig.server.json: migrated from `exclude` to the v9 `files`/`include` form required by the Ivy entry-point resolution.
src/main.ts: the v9 server-build migration added `export { renderModule, renderModuleFactory } from '@angular/platform-server';` (this file is the `server` target's main entry in angular.json).
Ran `ng update @ngrx/store@9`, which updated all five @ngrx packages and ran the router-store and effects v9 migrations.
package-lock.json regenerated by npm through `ng update`; verified with a clean `rm -rf node_modules && npm install`.
manual_followups: `npm test` fails at baseline and still fails, with the same cause: the karma target in angular.json lists `"styles": ["styles.css"]` instead of `"src/styles.css"`, so webpack cannot resolve the entry. Out of scope for this hop (pre-existing, not a regression), but worth fixing so the suite can actually run.

@nguniversal/module-map-ngfactory-loader is still pinned at 7.1.0 and warns about an incompatible @angular/platform-server peer. The browser build is unaffected; with Ivy the ModuleMapLoaderModule is obsolete and src/app/app.server.module.ts should eventually drop it (the @nguniversal packages are deprecated from v9 onward).

node-sass 4.11 (an optionalDependency) fails to compile on this Node 12 / Python 3 image and is skipped. Nothing in the build uses Sass, so it does not block anything, but it should be removed or replaced with `sass` in a later hop.
